business_problem: Rocket Money wanted to put a trustworthy financial expert in every customer's pocket, but a personal finance agent that reads account data, answers questions, and takes actions has to be highly accurate, observable, and cheap enough to scale.
solution_summary: Rocket Money built Rowan as an agent-workflow hybrid on the Claude Platform. User requests arrive by text message and first pass through a Haiku 4.5 classifier that routes each job to a single-responsibility subagent. Most subagents run on Sonnet 5, while Opus 5 handles the financial tasks that need deeper reasoning, and a final formatting agent keeps Rowan's voice consistent. Routine tasks stay deterministic code; when a website changes, a repair agent updates the automation instead of leaving the flow broken. The full system runs through Amazon Bedrock on top of Rocket Money's existing app and data services, with every failure traceable to the exact classifier or downstream call that failed. Claude Code and Fable also accelerated development, letting a small team ship and maintain many specialized agents in parallel.

data_flow: Customers text Rowan, a Haiku 4.5 classifier routes each request, Sonnet 5 or Opus 5 subagents execute the task against Rocket Money's finance workflows and app data, a formatter standardizes the reply, and deterministic code paths or repair agents handle external-site automations. Everything runs on Claude through Amazon Bedrock with traceable failures.
